nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Rillik. I keep the flood records here. The water has provided rather more material than my shelves were designed for.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: You can see the marks from this dry overlook. We need not step into the pool to read what it left behind.

choices.text: Can you tell how old they are?
Do you enjoy keeping the records?

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: They record where water reached, and where a reply was left. At least, that is what the surviving paired records suggest.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The first scratch can be older than the clear one beside it. Weather wears a surface unevenly. A tidy line is not always a recent line.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: I like the work. I am less certain that I always explain it usefully. Please stop me if I start describing the drawer instead of the record.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: We can look at one thing at a time. The pool will continue being a pool while we do.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Clear dawn makes the shallow scratches easier to see. I record the light as well as the mark, so I remember what helped me read it.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The morning rain darkens the rock. We can still compare the marks from under the roof. The paper need not join the weather.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Good day. I found the note I was looking for. It was beneath my note about where I had put it.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Rain is an observation, not an interruption. Wet paper, on the other hand, is a practical difficulty. The shelf here is dry.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The sun has left the lower mark. I copied it earlier, but I enjoy looking at the stone after the measurements are finished.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The evening rain is loud at the lip of the pool. We can read the rubbing here without having to speak over it.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The pool looks deeper at night. That is an impression, so I keep it separate from the measured depth.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: A wet night. The archive roof is doing its oldest and most useful piece of research: keeping these pages dry.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: There is a low flood mark I would like another pair of eyes on. Will you compare it with my rubbing from the dry overlook?

choices.text: I will compare the mark with you.
I will return for a closer look.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Thank you. Meet me at the plunge-pool overlook. We will compare the stone and paper without leaving the dry route.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Of course. I will keep the rubbing flat. An unanswered question is allowed to remain a question for a while.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The dry overlook beside the plunge pool is our starting point. No climb or water crossing is needed.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: From this overlook, the low mark is visible beside the older line. Would you like to compare the rubbing with what you can actually see?

choices.text: What can the rubbing tell us?

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The rubbing captures a surface, not its whole history. We should notice where it is faint rather than fill the gap with a confident guess.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Look at the low mark from this dry position, then use the comparison point to put my rubbing beside it. We can talk about what matches.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Compare the low mark and its rubbing at the overlook when you are ready. We do not need to get closer to the water.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: You compared the two. The long scratch matches; the short end fades on both stone and paper. Shall we keep that uncertainty in the record?

choices.text: Yes. We can leave the uncertain part clear.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Then it is an honest record. Keep this copy of the flood rubbing. A visible gap is more useful than a certainty we invented.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: I have written that the short end is unclear. It took fewer words than my earlier attempt to explain it away.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Nacri asked where the answer would go. I have left a place beside the first note. The drawer can manage one more page.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: You need not bring a question every time. I sometimes discover what I am thinking by having someone nearby who is not another shelf.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: You were willing to leave a gap in the record. I trust a friend who can say what they have not seen.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: That makes it easier for me to do the same. I have quite a number of unfinished observations, as it turns out.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: I have a new note, if you would like to hear it. Or we could let the water keep the conversation for a while.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The gathering held more answers than any single notice. I am glad you were there when I began understanding the difference.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: There are old records I have never made sense of. I would enjoy looking at them with you, without promising a discovery.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: I know I can bring you an uncertain thought. That is a surprisingly steady thing to know.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The old gathering notice records an arrival but gives little room to the reply. We should find out what changed before copying it again.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Both halves are now in the shared plan. The clear sky may suit one arrival; the sheltered ground display suits another.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Rain is included in the plan this time. The notice does not need the weather to agree with it before it can be useful.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: I recorded when the first lamp was lit. Then I stopped writing down arrival times. People continued to be welcome without my help.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Avren's upstream notes are very clear. I must remember to send a clear answer, rather than merely file them clearly.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Quillip has left a blank place on the map. Apparently it contains a bench. A respectable use of blankness.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: This rubbing is dry. I have checked three times. The third inspection has added very little to our knowledge.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: These old marks come in pairs. Will you look at both with me, from the dry overlook?

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Visit the plunge-pool overlook and inspect the two flood marks. Keep to the dry path. There is no need to enter the water.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: I will leave my rubbing flat. The rock has waited longer than either of us.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The two marks are read together. Inspect each from the dry overlook, then bring me what you noticed.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Yes. The upper mark records water arriving. The lower one records the reply sent to the next settlement.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The low mark you helped me read has a companion. The arrival above and the reply below complete the pair.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: I thought the second mark was a correction. It was a conversation. Even stone can leave room for an answer.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Selvie has the present notice at the silk awning. Let's find out whether its reply ever reached this side.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: The stone was not asking us to hold the water still. It was asking us to tell each other when it moved.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: Pool keepers who needed their neighbors to know what the water was doing. The smallest strokes were the acknowledgements.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: I'll add today's note on a loose card. The old stone stays as it is.

nodes.speaker: rillik
nodes.text: You already helped me hear the smaller mark. Together, the pair shows how an observation became a conversation.
